searchText: if a 51% attack is carried out successfully on ETH1.0 with the introduction of EIP-1558, how would that affect validators proposing blocks with a split network on what the canonical head of ETH1 is? EIP-1559* > if a 51% attack is carried out successfully on ETH1.0 with the introduction of EIP-1558, how would that affect validators proposing blocks with a split network on what the canonical head of ETH1 is? <@489217181104734219> again it’s not happening and not anywhere near happening Still the question remains, <@489217181104734219> what would probably happen if there is a big fork on eth1 is that there will not be majority on eth 2 validators voting, as presumably some will be on one fork deeming the vote of the others invalid. If there is no fork however on eth1 then this problem wouldn't happen if the eth1 fork(s) was not more than the `ETH1_FOLLOW_DISTANCE`, eth2 would process deposits as normal If the fork exceeded that depth, eth2 and eth1 wrt deposits could become out of sync This represents a huge issue with eth1 (regardless of the eth2 link) and would be a signal that the mining environment is essentially broken

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content:
if the eth1 fork(s) was not more than the `ETH1_FOLLOW_DISTANCE`, eth2 would process deposits as normal
If the fork exceeded that depth, eth2 and eth1 wrt deposits could become out of sync

This represents a huge issue with eth1 (regardless of the eth2 link) and would be a signal that the mining environment is essentially broken
